ratings.reviewer_notes: Directly links low SMN in SMA motor neurons to complex I dysfunction, reduced ATP, increased ROS/protein carbonylation, and impaired translational initiation, with pyruvate rescue involving mTOR-dependent SMN synthesis.

Tests oxidative stress and mitochondrial bioenergetics as candidate consequences of SMN deficiency but finds little oxidative stress and no SMN-rescue effect on mitochondrial respiration in this iPSC system.
SMN knockdown directly produces ATP depletion, increased mitochondrial membrane potential, altered cytochrome-c oxidase activity and oxygen consumption, and elevated free radicals in neural cells.
Identifies altered mitochondrial-bioenergetic gene expression and early defects in respiration, redox balance, membrane potential, transport, and network morphology in SMA motor neurons.

Directly demonstrates that SMN deficiency impairs mitochondrial axonal transport, abundance, morphology, and membrane potential in human spinal motor neurons; NAC mitigates these defects and degeneration.

Defines a muscle pathway in which SMN loss causes lysosomal dysfunction and ineffective mitochondrial clearance, leading to accumulation of abnormal mitochondria with impaired complexes I/IV, respiration, and excess ROS.
Shows the reverse or feedback direction: oxidative stress associated with paraquat-induced mitochondrial dysfunction promotes aberrant SMN2 exon skipping, potentially further lowering functional SMN.

Treated SMA patient muscle shows loss of oxidative-phosphorylation machinery and mitochondrial DNA alongside stress and denervation, but the study does not establish a mechanistic pathway from SMN deficiency.
Focused review of how SMN loss affects mitochondrial function in neuronal and muscular systems, including affected mitochondrial transcripts and potential contributions to SMA progression.

Connects SMA progression to dysregulated mitochondrial turnover, autophagosome accumulation, PINK1/Parkin/BNIP3 signals, abnormal OPA1 splicing, and mitochondrial fragmentation; exercise and urolithin A improve these pathways.

Provides a direct mechanism in muscle: SMN regulates MYOD1 and miR-1/miR-206, and loss of this axis impairs mitochondrial metabolic maturation, survival, and myotube formation; miRNA supplementation rescues the defects.
